title: General Training Reading
subtitle: Three sections, everyday and work texts
summary: Know what each General Training section contains, scan short factual texts quickly, and handle the work vocabulary Section 2 is built on.

lesson.heading: The three sections
rows: up to five short factual texts
train timetable, shop advertisements, travel brochures
two work-related texts, descriptive and informational
staff-training manual, job description, job application procedures
one longer text, descriptive and instructive rather than argumentative
magazine article about modern travel, an extract from a novel
lesson.note: The sections get harder as you go, so Section 1 is the easiest and Section 3 the most difficult.

lesson.heading: Spend your hour unevenly
lesson.text: You have **60 minutes for 40 questions**, and you must transfer your answers within that time. Section 1 is the cheapest to answer, so finish it fast and bank the minutes for the harder sections.

examples.text: Section 1 - no more than **15-20 minutes**
Aim for **less than 20 minutes** per section so you have time to check at the end.

lesson.note: The same skills as the Academic paper - skimming, scanning, spotting paraphrase - are what make this possible.

lesson.heading: Recognise a text from one line of it
lesson.text: Short factual texts announce themselves. A single extract usually tells you what kind of document you are in, which tells you what sort of questions to expect.

examples.text: *The chosen applicant will have proven skills in problem solving ...*
*Passengers travelling into the city should change trains at Bardon.*
*Sick leave: any member of staff who is ill should immediately contact their department supervisor.*
*Your application form will be processed by the Human Resources team ...*
*When we finally arrived at the hotel we were too exhausted to notice just how run-down it was.*
*Opening Times: Weekdays 9:00-17:00 ...*

lesson.heading: Paraphrase works the same way here
lesson.note: Answers are almost never word-for-word. Where the text says *come and find out about our fascinating sea creatures*, the question asks about *animals*.

lesson.heading: The vocabulary of work
lesson.text: Section 2 is built on workplace language, so the words below repay learning directly. Many questions turn on knowing one of them.

examples.text: **hospitality** - the industry related to hotels and restaurants
**retail** - the industry related to shops
**redundancy** - the loss of a job due to a business closing
**retire** - to stop working, usually because of age
**consumer** - a person who uses goods; **customer** - a person who buys goods
**manual** - the type of work done with your hands
**shift** - a person's scheduled period of work
**employee** - a staff member; **employer** - the person who provides you with work
**deadline** - the time by which work must be completed
**recruit** - to hire or employ a person for a job

lesson.heading: Several short texts at once
lesson.text: Section 1 often gives you a handful of related texts - five college open-day advertisements, say - and asks which one contains a particular detail. Work from the question, scan all the texts for the detail, and do not read any one of them in full.

examples.text: *Which college offers a free flying lesson?*
*Which event runs into the evening?*
examples.note: Scan for times - *10:00 till 21:00* - and for *fireworks*.

lesson.text: Strategies alone will not get you the band you want. Keep building vocabulary and grammar alongside them - most lost marks in this paper are lost to a word the candidate did not know.

exercises.prompt: Match each General Training section with its theme.

pairs.right: Social survival - up to five short factual texts
General reading - one longer descriptive text

exercises.prompt: Match each work word with its meaning.

pairs.right: losing a job because the business closes
to hire someone for a job
the time by which work must be finished

exercises.prompt: *Sick leave: any member of staff who is ill and unable to come to work should immediately contact their department supervisor.* Which kind of text is this?
exercises.explanation: A rule addressed to staff about how to behave at work belongs in Section 2 - workplace survival.

exercises.statement: In General Training Reading you get extra time to transfer your answers onto the answer sheet.
exercises.explanation: The 60 minutes includes transferring. Aim for under 20 minutes per section so the transfer is not rushed.

exercises.prompt: Sort these words by who they describe.
categories: The person who uses or buys
The person who works or hires

exercises.prompt: Match the words in the text with the paraphrase used in the question.
A worker who stops working because of age is said to ___.
exercises.explanation: Compare *redundancy*, which is losing a job because the business closes - the cause is what separates them.

exercises.prompt: How long should you spend on Section 1?
exercises.explanation: It is the easiest section, so every minute saved there is a minute available for Sections 2 and 3.

exercises.statement: The Section 3 text in General Training is usually argumentative, like the Academic Section 3 passage.
exercises.explanation: It is one longer text that is descriptive and instructive rather than argumentative - a magazine article or a novel extract.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that describes what a shift is.
exercises.answer: A shift is a person's scheduled period of work.
exercises.explanation: Work vocabulary like this is tested directly in Section 2 - it is worth memorising the list.
